title: Homecoming and Yearbook
premise: Jonah Yarrow, the quiet statistician of Hollow Creek High's championship football team, discovers the school board has been falsifying eligibility records to keep star players on the field. Paired for a semester project with Priya Chandrasekaran — his academic rival and the coach's niece — he must decide whether to expose the fraud that funds his own scholarship path. As their uneasy alliance deepens into something like trust, and then love, Jonah learns the buried records also conceal how a former player's injury was covered up. In the end, Jonah testifies before the board with Priya beside him, sacrificing his scholarship and gaining instead a found family among the whistleblowers, teammates, and teachers who choose truth over the game.
about_author: Lena Ravensworth is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent three years covering high school athletics before turning to fiction. She writes young adult stories about quiet kids who refuse to stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Numbers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet Jonah in his element: compiling stats in the empty bleachers after Friday's win, invisible by design. He notices one anomaly — an ineligible player on the roster sheet — and files it away. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being nobody.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs him with Priya Chandrasekaran for the semester civics project on 'institutional accountability.' Their first meeting is pure friction; she thinks he's coasting, he thinks she's the coach's attack dog. Emotional beat: reluctant collision of two worlds.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals her own stake: her cousin Dev was injured playing for Hollow Creek two years ago and left without answers. She suspects the records were scrubbed. Jonah says nothing about what he saw. Emotional beat: grief worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Box Under the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Chasing a misfiled stat sheet into the athletic storage room, Jonah finds a locked filing cabinet labeled ARCHIVE 2019-2021 — the years that matter. He photographs the lock, heart hammering. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Jonah and Priya negotiate a truce over bad diner coffee: she'll bring access through her uncle, he'll bring the data. Neither mentions the cabinet. Emotional beat: wary respect taking root.

chapters.title: Rigged
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-referencing transfer dates against eligibility filings, Jonah proves three players played while ineligible — including the team captain. The pattern points upward, past the coach, to the board. Emotional beat: the sick thrill of confirmation.

chapters.title: What Uncle Marcus Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya probes Coach Marcus gently at Sunday dinner; he deflects, but his hands shake. She realizes he may be complicit — or trapped. Emotional beat: love complicated by suspicion.

chapters.title: Dev's Last Game
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah pulls the footage of Dev's injury and finds the play happened during a timeout that never existed in the official log — evidence erased. He shows Priya. Emotional beat: shared horror forging real partnership.

chapters.title: Midterm Warning
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The pair presents preliminary findings; Ms. Okafor praises them privately, then warns them: 'Some doors are load-bearing. Know which ones you're opening.' That night Jonah's locker is pried open. Emotional beat: the cost of looking.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Letter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A state university offers Jonah a full ride — contingent on a glowing recommendation from the athletic department. Exposing the board could kill it. His mother, exhausted from double shifts, tells him to take the money. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience made flesh.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Out
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, Jonah, Ms. Okafor, and retired teacher Mr. Bell — who kept copies of the original 2020 files — form an informal circle meeting in Bell's garage. For the first time Jonah feels he belongs somewhere. Emotional beat: warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. An anonymous note threatens Jonah's mother's job at the district office. The captain confronts him in the parking lot — not with fists, but fear: 'If I can't play, I don't eat.' Emotional beat: realizing the guilty and the desperate are entangled.

chapters.title: The Cabinet Opens
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Using a key Mr. Bell never surrendered, they open the archive: Dev's medical reports, altered transcripts, and a memo signed by board president Ellen Voss reading 'manage the narrative.' Emotional beat: proof in hand, terror rising.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Homecoming week erupts around them — pep rallies, banners, Coach Marcus honored at halftime. Priya watches the town celebrate the lie and understands what exposure will destroy. Jonah asks her to the dance; she says yes. Emotional beat: tenderness inside complicity.

chapters.title: One Night Off
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the dance, under paper stars, Jonah and Priya stop being partners-investigation and become partners, period. Then Voss approaches, all smiles, offering Jonah anything he wants. He declines. Emotional beat: love declared as the walls close in.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The garage copies vanish; Mr. Bell is hospitalized after a 'fall.' Ms. Okafor is reassigned mid-semester. The project itself is cancelled by administrative order. Emotional beat: the machine striking back.

chapters.title: Coach Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Cornered by Priya's questions and his own guilt, Marcus confesses: he altered the logs under orders after Dev's injury, believing he was protecting the program. He agrees to testify — if they go first. Emotional beat: a broken man choosing truth.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The board meets Thursday to vote on renewing Voss's contract — after which the archive will be legally destroyed. With the scholarship letter due Friday, Jonah must choose by Wednesday night. He withdraws his application. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Before a packed gymnasium, Jonah presents the data, Priya presents the documents, Marcus testifies, and Dev — in a wheelchair, invited by Priya — speaks last. Voss resigns mid-session. Emotional beat: catharsis; the quiet kid finally heard.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The fallout is messy: the season vacated, the town furious, some friendships gone. But Ms. Okafor returns, Bell recovers, and a district oversight committee forms — with student seats. Emotional beat: grief and repair coexisting.

chapters.title: Yearbook
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Yearbook signing day. Priya writes in Jonah's copy: 'You were never under the radar. You were the signal.' They plan a future neither scholarship nor scandal dictated. Emotional beat: love and identity affirmed.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Again
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue. One year later, Jonah — now interning with the state auditor thanks to Bell's old contacts — returns for the homecoming game where Dev, coaching youth league, throws him the ceremonial first pass. Emotional beat: full-circle belonging; inheritance redefined as truth passed forward.
